analysis: Late-morning tape (8:00–9:00 AM PT): the morning split into two halves. Early trade was risk-off as the 10Y re-pressured equities — opening gains faded — then indexes reversed higher late morning on Hormuz peace hopes: Dow +0.4%, S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.3%, while the Russell 2000 slipped -0.2%, erasing its early gains. The 10Y sits at 5.21%, right on yesterday's 2007 intraday-high territory — the two live outlets disagree on the day change (IBD live: +5 bps; Investopedia: <1 bps), which is itself a signal of how twitchy the bond tape is. The AI demand bid keeps confirming from hard sources: Musk's xAI post (220k GB300 Blackwell by November, another 220k possible by late December, 1M-chip target) is a primary-source datapoint that kept NVDA above its 21-day line, and Akamai's +7% on the confirmed $11.6B Anthropic contract (plus $9B expansion option) is real committed revenue, not rumor. MU/SNDK edging higher fits the memory-pricing read-through ahead of MU earnings Sept 30. Counterweights: META -3% even after the $865 Cowen target — the validation note can't beat the rotation — and oil's relief (WTI back below $94) still prices a 7-day Hormuz roadmap whose conditions remain single-source and disputed. What changed vs 8 AM: index moves are now late-morning reversals rather than mid-morning drift; the Musk post is new primary demand data; AKAM's $9B expansion option is a new confirmed detail; and the 10Y's day-change is disputed, so treat any single yield read as fragile. Signal vs noise: index moves, yield level, Musk post, AKAM deal terms, WTI/Brent moves are confirmed; the Islamabad MOU conditions and Hormuz 7-day terms remain single-source/unconfirmed — fragile. A/D, volume vs 20-day, and precise VIX change remain unavailable from sourced pages.

headlines.headline: Opening gains faded on rising yields, then indexes reversed higher late morning on U.S.-Iran peace hopes: Dow +0.4%, S&P 500 +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.3% (it flirted with negative earlier); the small-cap Russell 2000 erased its early gains and turned -0.2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A reversal, not a trend: the bid came back only after yields stopped rising intraday — the tape is still yield-hostage, so the bounce is reversible if the 10Y re-tests Thursday's 2007 intraday high.

headlines.headline: Late Thursday, SpaceX's Elon Musk posted on X that the xAI Memphis data center already houses 'several' of Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell chips and expects another 220,000 GB300 Blackwell chips by November ('If we get lucky, yet another 220k GB300 by late December'), toward a target of 1 million chips. NVDA edged 0.1% lower but held above its 21-day moving average; SpaceX -0.9%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Primary-source demand data for Blackwell: a single customer talking about adding 440k+ flagship chips in ~3 months is the concrete order-flow behind the AI tape, which is why NVDA held a key technical level on a down day.

headlines.headline: Akamai (AKAM) surged ~7% mid-morning, rebounding off its 50-day moving average, on the confirmed Anthropic deal: at least $11.6B over seven years for cloud infrastructure and software, with a potential $9B expansion. The morning's three upgrades (Piper $158, Guggenheim $225, Evercore 'landmark') already framed it as confirmed hard revenue.
headlines.why_it_matters: Committed multi-billion revenue with an expansion option — the deal keeps anchoring the AI-demand leg of the week, and the hold above the 50-day line after the spike shows the bid is sticking rather than being faded.

headlines.headline: Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK) edged higher in the late-morning trade. Micron earnings are due Sept 30 — the next hard catalyst for the memory/pricing read-through the AI hardware bid is pricing.
headlines.why_it_matters: Memory names moving with the AI-infrastructure bid ahead of MU's print means next week's earnings land against an already-loaded tape — good numbers extend the bid, any miss lands harder.

headlines.headline: WTI slipped 0.8% to below $94/bbl and Brent fell ~0.5% to ~$106 on the Hormuz-reopening hopes. Iran's FM Araghchi said the Strait would open 'at the end of seven days' and nuclear talks restart if conditions already in June's 14-point Islamabad MOU are met (halt to fighting, open Hormuz to all ship traffic, Iran vow not to develop nuclear weapons). No White House confirmation of the terms; Trump keeps the blockade until nuclear issues are addressed.
headlines.why_it_matters: Oil's relief is real in price terms, but it prices a 7-day roadmap that rests on disputed single-source terms — the MOU detail gives it a shape, yet one denial from either side reverses the move, so treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Meta fell 3% in morning action — one of the Nasdaq-100's biggest losers alongside INTC (-1%+) — even after TD Cowen's $865 target lift on the Muse revenue call (stock on 5th straight weekly gain, <1% from the $2T line). Nasdaq-100 winners early were ARM and DDOG, +5% each.
headlines.why_it_matters: The analyst validation note is not beating the rotation: META cooling on a +5-week run shows megacap gains are being selectively trimmed into strength even with bullish targets — a caution flag on chasing the month's biggest winner.

market_snapshot.notes: 10Y at 5.21% — Investopedia: up <1 bps from Thursday's close, +~21 bps on the week, fresh 2007 intraday high yesterday; IBD live: +5 bps intraday. Disputed day change, so treated as a level (5.21%) rather than a move. VIX: Barron's had it just over 15 early Friday, down ~1/3 pt; closed Thursday at 15.67. Gold $4,265.30 (-0.2%) after the Michigan inflation-expectations jump. BTC ~$84,000. Michigan final 48.1 and core capex +1.6% (8 AM data) carried: October-hike case still alive.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning (verified across search; last announcements remain the Sept 9/10 items: $600M 6.75% senior notes pricing due 2035 with ~$592M net to repay credit borrowings, and the NYSE-to-TXSE listing transfer — NYSE trading ends Oct 2, TXSE begins Oct 5, ticker unchanged). Carried: Q2 revenue $342.1M, adjusted EBITDA $193.2M, DCF coverage 1.65x, $0.525 distribution, FY guidance confirmed (EBITDA $770-800M, DCF $480-510M). Units trade into a softer oil tape (WTI below $94, Brent ~$106 on unconfirmed Hormuz deal talk), a modest near-term sector tailwind.

watch_next: Does the 10Y hold at 5.21% or re-test Thursday's 2007 intraday high into the close — still the single biggest constraint on Friday's finish.
2:00 PM ET: Cleveland Fed's Hammack speaks — watch for October-commitment language; Evercore reads Williams' Thursday remarks as leaning against an October hike without ruling it out.
Does AKAM hold its +7% morning gains into the close on the $9B expansion-option detail, and does META stabilize toward the $2T line after -3%.
Any confirmation or denial of the Hormuz 7-day roadmap / Islamabad MOU terms — the swing factor for oil, inflation expectations, and the tape into next week.
Micron earnings Sept 30 and Oct 27-28 FOMC are the next hard catalysts.
